original.target_description: Stelzl, Janes, and Seligman, Champ or chump: strategic utilization of dual social identities of others, Study 2. Full primary paper could not be acquired through permitted free routes; target test not inspected.

replication.target_description: French conceptual analogue of original Canadianness contrast: nationality ratings after victory versus defeat exclusively in the shared French-English identity condition; manuscript p. 7 simple effect.

n.sample_role: Participants in shared-win (30) and shared-loss (26) conditions for the simple contrast; the test uses the full 114-participant ANOVA error term.
n.exclusions: None: all participants passed manipulation checks and no participants were excluded.
n.location: Manuscript p. 4, Participants and design; p. 6, Preliminary analyses and manipulation checks

es.location: Manuscript p. 7, Perception of Frank Williams’s nationality, simple effect in shared identity condition

p.location: Manuscript p. 7, Perception of Frank Williams’s nationality, simple effect in shared identity condition

reported_success.quote: The results generally replicate those of prior research

notes: Original and replication assessed independently. Replication is an explicitly stated conceptual replication of Study 2, adapting Canadian-American/Belgian-American high jumping to French-English/Belgian-English judo. The author narrative verdict is paper-level and qualified by generally; it is not inferred from the target p value. Replication text is a frozen parse of publicly accessible author-uploaded full HTML, with title and DOI verified; PDF links were inaccessible. Greek eta is rendered as g in this parse. The n field preserves the two printed condition sizes separately; no combined contrast N is printed. France is the planned replication analogue of Canada.
